name: Palantir Technologies

summary.text: Palantir Technologies is a publicly traded data-analytics and software company. Peter Thiel, Alex Karp and Stephen Cohen are among its co-founders. Thiel has chaired its board since 2003, and Karp has been CEO since 2005. The CIA's venture arm In-Q-Tel was an early investor. Its software is used by U.S. defense, intelligence and law enforcement agencies, including ICE.

facts.claim: In-Q-Tel, the CIA's venture capital arm, made an early equity investment in Palantir. Michael Steinberger's 2025 book puts it at $1.25 million. Palantir engineers worked directly with CIA analysts as they developed the software, and the CIA later became a customer.

sources.publisher: Fast Company South Africa (excerpt from Michael Steinberger, The Philosopher in the Valley, Avid Reader Press)
sources.title: The evolution of Palantir from CIA investments to police partnerships

facts.claim: Palantir built FALCON, a database and analytics platform used by ICE's Homeland Security Investigations, and in 2014 won a $41 million contract to build ICE's Investigative Case Management system (The Intercept, 2017). In January 2026, 404 Media reported that ICE uses a Palantir-built app called ELITE to map potential deportation targets.

sources.title: Palantir Provides the Engine for Donald Trump's Deportation Machine
'ELITE': The Palantir App ICE Uses to Find Neighborhoods to Raid

facts.claim: In April 2025 ICE awarded Palantir roughly $30 million (reported as $29.8 million to $30 million) to deliver the Immigration Lifecycle Operating System ('ImmigrationOS') prototype by September 25, 2025. An ICE spokesperson said the deal was a modification to an existing contract; Business Insider reported it extends a 2022 operations-and-maintenance contract, and the justification document cited an 'urgent and compelling' need and named Palantir as the only source able to deliver in time.
facts.quote: ICE awarded Palantir a $30 million contract to deliver a new platform, the Immigration Lifecycle Operating System, by Sept. 25, per federal records.

sources.title: ICE just ordered $30 million worth of new technology from Palantir to track immigrants
Palantir Lands ICE Contract for ImmigrationOS Support
Palantir granted $30 million to build ImmigrationOS surveillance platform for ICE
Palantir's partnership with ICE deepens

facts.claim: In 2025 ICE published a sole-source notice for the next version of its Investigative Case Management (ICM) system, inviting industry feedback through June 20, 2025, stating that only Palantir could meet the performance, security and integration standards needed to deploy the next iteration of ICM by a September 2026 deadline. A second task order of about $29.9 million for ImmigrationOS software licenses, operations and maintenance followed in September 2025.
facts.quote: ICE concluded that only Palantir could meet the high-performance, high-security, and integration standards necessary to deploy the next iteration of ICM by its critical September 2026 deadline.

sources.title: ICE advances sole source deal with Palantir for new surveillance backbone
Palantir granted $30 million to build ImmigrationOS surveillance platform for ICE

facts.claim: The Project On Government Oversight reported in June 2025 that White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller's OGE Form 278e financial disclosure, released by the White House, listed between $100,001 and $250,000 of Palantir stock held in a brokerage account for one of his minor children, and that at least 11 other White House officials and staffers also reported owning Palantir stock. The White House said Miller had confirmed to ethics officials that he would recuse from official matters that could affect those stocks.
facts.quote: Miller disclosed from $100,001 up to a quarter million dollars of stock in Palantir, a tech company woven into the operations of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

sources.title: Stephen Miller's Conflicts of Interest
Stephen Miller, New Entrant Public Financial Disclosure Report

facts.claim: On July 31, 2025 the U.S. Army announced a 10-year Enterprise Agreement with Palantir with a ceiling of up to $10 billion, consolidating 75 existing contracts (15 prime and 60 related) into one. The Army said the $10 billion was the maximum potential value, not a commitment, and that the deal set volume-based discounts and removed reseller pass-through fees.
facts.quote: The Army is consolidating 75 contracts into a single enterprise agreement with Palantir that will last for 10 years and have a ceiling of up to $10 billion.

sources.title: Palantir signs $10B enterprise agreement with Army
U.S. Army Awards Palantir Potential $10 Billion Contract
$10 billion, 10 year US Army contract elevates Palantir to defense contracting royalty

facts.claim: In May 2025 the Defense Department raised the ceiling of Palantir's Maven Smart System contract by $795 million, to nearly $1.3 billion through 2029, citing increased use of the system by combatant commands. An Army official told DefenseScoop the ceiling was raised in anticipation of future demand and that no acquisition decisions had been made.
facts.quote: raise the contract ceiling for Palantir's MSS to nearly $1.3 billion through 2029

sources.title: DOD raises Palantir Maven Smart System contract ceiling
Maven Smart System contract W911QX24D0012

facts.claim: Palantir held its first board meeting of 2024 in Tel Aviv in January 2024. The company announced the meeting on social media as a show of solidarity with Israel, about three months into the war with Hamas, and wrote that its work in the region had never been more vital. CEO Alex Karp said at Tel Aviv University that one reason for bringing the board was to embarrass people who back Israel in private but not in public.
facts.quote: among the reasons for bringing the board to Israel was to embarrass people who back Israel in private but not in public

sources.title: US tech giant Palantir decides to hold first board meeting of new year in Tel Aviv
US Palantir CEO flies company board to Israel in show of solidarity
Tech giant Palantir to hold first board meeting of 2024 in Israel

facts.claim: Bloomberg reported in January 2024 that Palantir agreed a 'strategic partnership' with Israel's Ministry of Defense to supply technology for its military efforts, following a meeting in Tel Aviv between Israeli defense officials and co-founders Peter Thiel and Alex Karp. In 2025 Calcalist reported that Norwegian asset manager Storebrand divested about $24 million of Palantir shares, citing the company's Israel contracts.
facts.quote: the agreement followed a Thursday meeting between Israeli defense officials and Palantir co-founders Peter Thiel and Alex Karp in Tel Aviv

sources.title: Thiel's Palantir, Israel Agree Strategic Partnership for Battle Tech
Palantir supplying Israel with technology to help in war effort
Palantir's Israel contracts prompt $24M Storebrand divestment over rights concerns

facts.claim: In March 2024 Alex Karp told CNBC that Palantir had lost employees, and expected to lose more, over his public support for Israel, and that after October 7 the company was 'on the ground and involved in operationally crucial work in Israel'.
facts.quote: after October 7, the company was on the ground and involved in operationally crucial work in Israel

sources.title: Palantir CEO says his outspoken pro-Israel views have caused employees to leave company
Palantir CEO stands firm in support of Israel despite employee departures

facts.claim: In a clip from the Hill and Valley Forum, reported by Israel Hayom as filmed in April 2025 and resurfacing in September 2025, a protester told Karp that Palantir's technology kills Palestinians; Karp replied 'Mostly terrorists, that's true' and described the protester as a useful idiot for Hamas.
facts.quote: "Mostly terrorists, that's true," Karp deadpanned, to applause.

sources.title: Watch: Palantir's Alex Karp shuts down pro-Palestinian heckler in resurfaced clip

facts.claim: In April 2025 WIRED reported that DOGE representatives, several Palantir staff and dozens of career IRS engineers had spent three days building a 'mega API', a single data-access layer above all IRS databases, with DOGE wanting Palantir's Foundry to become the 'read center' of IRS systems. A Treasury spokesperson told WIRED that no contract had been signed and that many vendors were being considered, Palantir among them.
facts.quote: For the last three days, DOGE and a handful of Palantir representatives, along with dozens of career IRS engineers, have been collaborating to build a "mega API," WIRED has learned.

sources.title: DOGE and Palantir representatives collaborating with IRS engineers to build a 'mega API'
DOGE reportedly planning a hackathon to build 'mega API' for IRS data
DOGE Reportedly Plans to Construct 'Mega API' in IRS 'Hackathon'

connections.claim: Jacob Helberg, described in coverage of his nomination as a senior adviser to Palantir CEO Alex Karp, was confirmed by the Senate as Under Secretary of State for Economic Growth, Energy, and the Environment on October 7, 2025 by 51-47 (roll call 547), after a Senate Foreign Relations Committee hearing on June 10, 2025. Sludge reported that he planned to keep investments in hundreds of companies.

openQuestions: The ImmigrationOS award value is reported as $29.8M or $30M; confirm on USAspending (reported contract ID 70CTD022FR0000170) and the SAM.gov justification. The page's description of the award as 'no-bid' corresponds to the limited-source justification reported here.
The page's '$15M Super PAC' link runs through Peter Thiel and JD Vance, not Palantir; see peter-thiel.json and jd-vance.json.
Whether Palantir was subsequently contracted for the IRS 'mega API' after the April 2025 WIRED report was not determined this session.

The Karp 'Mostly terrorists' exchange is dated to April 2025 by Israel Hayom and the Free Beacon, but a Substack post dates a similar protest to 2024; the original Hill and Valley Forum video would settle the date.
The Army's own release on the $10 billion Enterprise Agreement (army.mil) was not opened; the facts rest on trade-press reports of it.
